_doc_note: Shape per the OpenAI Responses API web search guide, https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-web-search, read 2026-10-05. Confirmed there: a search is an output item of type web_search_call (id, status, action), and with include=['web_search_call.action.sources'] its action.sources returns the complete list of URLs the model consulted, unlike the inline citations; answer text parts of type output_text carry url_citation annotations with url, title, start_index, end_index. The Responses API reference (https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/responses/methods/create) gives each source entry as {type: url, url}, and gives the open_page and find_in_page actions (which the guide lists for reasoning models) a url field. The guide shows no usage block; usage.input_tokens and usage.output_tokens are the ResponseUsage field names in the official openai-python SDK types (src/openai/types/responses/response_usage.py), read the same day. Hand-written from those shapes, not a live capture.
